context.title: Mahoney and Kaktus, NoiseTracker V1.0 documentation
context.note: Original July–August 1989 text, improvement list, corrected loop values, song commands and replay-source instructions. Preserved at https://github.com/cmatsuoka/tracker-history/blob/master/reference/amiga/noisetracker/NoiseTracker.doc

context.title: Mahoney and Kaktus, NoiseTracker 2.0 NormalReplay V1.1
context.note: Original E.A.S. 1990 replay code; sample initialisation, pattern reading and effect routines. https://github.com/cmatsuoka/tracker-history/blob/master/reference/amiga/noisetracker/NormalReplay.S

context.title: Amiga Computing 43, Octa MEDley
context.note: December 1991 review of OctaMED 2 by Jason Holborn; score editing and composition workflow. Separate contemporary advertisements identify the edition’s MIDI features.

context.title: CU Amiga, MED supplement
context.note: October 1991, Mat Broomfield feature on MED and OctaMED 2.00; editor structure and Teijo Kinnunen credit.

context.title: Teijo Kinnunen, OctaMEDPlayer guide
context.note: Original player documentation, copyright 1991–1996: supported songs, mixing modes, CPU/quality trade-offs and author/publisher credits. https://files.mpoli.fi/unpacked/software/misc/amiga/omedplay.lha/octamedplayer.guide

context.title: Urban Jonsson, FastTracker v2.08 manual
context.note: February 1996; programmers’ introduction by Fredrik Huss and Magnus Högdahl; sections 4.1 and 4.2 on patterns and instruments. https://milkytracker.org/docs/FT2.pdf

context.title: Mr. H of Triton, XM format description
context.note: Original 1994 format document, preserved in libxmp; instrument/sample maps, envelopes, pattern order and sample data. The document contains version inconsistencies, so no universal byte-level specification is inferred. https://github.com/libxmp/libxmp/blob/master/docs/formats/xm.txt

context.title: 8bitbubsy, ft2-clone README
context.note: Current maintainer distinguishes the modern clone and its changes from the original DOS program. https://github.com/8bitbubsy/ft2-clone

context.title: Sami Tammilehto, Scream Tracker 3.20 TECH.DOC
context.note: Original official format/mixing document: channel assignments, sample and AdLib headers, packed patterns, version flags and mixer. Preserved at https://github.com/reznet/S3MParser/blob/master/TECH.DOC

context.title: PC Review, Scream Tracker review
context.note: August 1992: contemporary coverage of an earlier four-channel edition and a printer-port audio board; not evidence of ST3 features.

context.title: Jeffrey Lim, Impulse Tracker manual
context.note: Section 1.2 and 2.7 describe the predecessor’s keyboard workflow and why the later program followed it. https://github.com/jthlim/impulse-tracker/blob/main/ReleaseDocumentation/IT.TXT

context.title: Jeffrey Lim, Impulse Tracker User’s Manual
context.note: Original IT.TXT, sections 1.2, 2.2 and 2.5: keyboard interface, sample/instrument modes and new-note actions. https://github.com/jthlim/impulse-tracker/blob/main/ReleaseDocumentation/IT.TXT

context.title: Jeffrey Lim, ITTECH.TXT
context.note: Original format description: instrument and sample headers, envelope fields, channel data and playback flags. https://github.com/jthlim/impulse-tracker/blob/main/ReleaseDocumentation/ITTECH.TXT

context.title: Jeffrey Lim, Impulse Tracker source README
context.note: Author’s repository explains the 2014 source release, included drivers and historical rather than actively developed status. https://github.com/jthlim/impulse-tracker

context.title: Lasse Öörni and contributors, GoatTracker 2.77 readme
context.note: Original project manual, sections 3 and 5: instrument tables, packer/relocator, player integration and options. https://svn.code.sf.net/p/goattracker2/code/goattrk2/trunk/readme.txt

context.title: Cadaver, tools catalogue
context.note: Creator-maintained distinction between host-side editor and C64 tweak utility; audio backends and version differences. https://cadaver.github.io/tools.html

context.title: Dag Lem, reSID README and AUTHORS
context.note: Original project description and author credit; cycle-based engine, filter model, VICE and SIDPLAY integration. https://github.com/libsidplayfp/resid/blob/master/README https://github.com/libsidplayfp/resid/blob/master/AUTHORS

context.title: Dag Lem, reSID envelope.cc
context.note: Original implementation and measurement comments for envelope rates and delayed transitions; explanations distinguish observed measurements and hypotheses. https://github.com/libsidplayfp/resid/blob/master/envelope.cc

context.title: VICE manual, SID settings
context.note: Consumer documentation explains reSID sampling methods, chip models and filter-bias settings. https://vice-emu.sourceforge.io/vice_7.html

context.title: Amiga Computing, TFMX review
context.note: November 1990, pp. 120–121: pattern editing, macros controlling sample behaviour, pitch effects, a separate player and no supplied replay source. Original page 121 consulted.

context.title: Dean Friedman, TFMX Soundtool, AmigaWorld
context.note: October 1990, pp. 106–107: contemporary review, editor/player arrangement and reviewer-reported faults.

context.title: The Games Machine 27, TFMX and X-Out
context.note: February 1990: contemporary report on Hülsbeck’s development and game use.

context.title: Chris Hülsbeck, In the Chair, Retro Gamer 115
context.note: June 2013, pp. 90–94: retrospective account of Jochen Hippel and the later seven-voice Turrican II system; not a claim about every retail TFMX edition.

context.title: The One 43, public-domain pages
context.note: April 1992, p. 67: Voyage identified as 17-Bit disk 1604, with the contents described for prospective buyers.

context.title: Amiga Format 37, Top ten demos of the month
context.note: August 1992, p. 186: 17-Bit library chart, with Hardwired, Odyssey and Voyage/Voyager; a library sales list, not a census of all Amiga owners.

context.title: Allister Brimble interview, Amiga Format 103
context.note: November 1997, pp. 20–21: retrospective account of submitting music to 17-Bit and the later Team17 connection.

context.title: Fred Fish, ReadMeFirst and Distribution
context.note: Original library notes revised 24 December 1990; start in November 1985, intended users, selection criteria and compilation-copyright disclaimer. https://www.funet.fi/pub/amiga/fish/FredsInfo/ReadMeFirst https://www.funet.fi/pub/amiga/fish/FredsInfo/Distribution

context.title: Amiga Freely Redistributable Library, Contents
context.note: Original collection catalogue: disk 47 Juggler credit; disks 189/190 NetHack 2.3 distribution, source and Amiga port credit. https://www.funet.fi/pub/amiga/fish/Contents

context.title: Amiga Computing, Fred Fish public-domain coverage
context.note: June 1991, p. 27: contemporary discussion of collection size, international contributions and Aquarium catalogue searching.

context.title: Julian Rignall, Compunet, ZZAP!64 26
context.note: June 1987, p. 73: contemporary directory recommendations and Man on the Moon credits; describes actual shared demos rather than a modern reconstruction.

context.title: Nosher, Commodore communications-modem history
context.note: Secondary contextual article accompanying the December 1985 Commodore Computing International advert; corroborates the modem/service context, not the specific 1987 demo credits. https://nosher.net/archives/computers/adve_085?idx=Popular+Computing+Weekly

context.title: Acorn User 9, Micro database links to Prestel
context.note: April 1983 news: reported March launch, joining/annual charges, modem login, telesoftware and access to broader Prestel pages.

context.title: Viewdata and Teletext, volume 6 number 1, Netting personal computer
context.note: Contemporary launch-period coverage and Micronet advertising: Prestel infrastructure and computer-owner services. https://www.viewdata.org.uk/download.php?cat=15_Prestel&file=vatu-v6i1-p8.pdf

context.title: Micronet advertisement, Your Computer
context.note: June 1985, p. 30: identity number/password and services. https://nosher.net/archives/computers/your_computer_1985-06_030

context.title: Homebrew Computer Club Newsletter, volume 2 number 3
context.note: 31 March 1976, p. 1: first meeting, organisers, attendance, newsletter distribution and meeting format. https://bitsavers.computerhistory.org/pdf/homebrewCC/HCC_Newsletter_V2_N03.pdf

context.title: Homebrew Computer Club Newsletter 3
context.note: 10 May 1975: San Francisco chapter, practical assistance, information indexing and Lee Felsenstein’s chairing role. https://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/access/text/2015/02/102740021-05-03-acc.pdf

context.title: Len Shustek, The Homebrew Computer Club 2013 Reunion
context.note: Participant account, CHM, 17 December 2013: garage meeting, SLAC venue, mapping/random-access periods and Wozniak’s demonstrations. https://computerhistory.org/blog/the-homebrew-computer-club-2013-reunion/

context.title: ICPUG North Herts, A Short History
context.note: Regional group’s own historical account: PET origins, name changes, volunteer journal, benefits and distinction between national closure and regional continuation. https://icpug-northherts.yolasite.com/history.php

context.title: Amiga Shopper 11, User Groups directory
context.note: March 1992, pp. 150–151: Biggin Hill lectures/open help evenings and regional entries.

context.title: Commodore Scene 23, ICPUG closure notice
context.note: Late-1998 issue quotes chairman John Blackstaff on the national group closing at year end and no 1999 renewals. https://files.commodore.software/reference-material/newsletters/commodore-scene/commodore-scene-issue-23.pdf

context.title: No-Intro project home page
context.note: Project’s own description: catalogues best available copies, provides DAT files and an online database; does not distribute the listed software. https://no-intro.org/

context.title: No-Intro, Naming Convention
context.note: Original project convention for titles, regions, language, revisions, prototypes and other record fields. https://wiki.no-intro.org/index.php?title=Naming_Convention

context.title: No-Intro, Nintendo DSi Digital CDN DAT notes
context.note: Documented example of fields including size, CRC32, MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-256; used as an example of record structure, not a claim that every platform uses all fields. https://wiki.no-intro.org/index.php?title=Nintendo_-_Nintendo_DSi_%28Digital%29_%28CDN%29_dat_notes

context.title: No-Intro, DAT-o-MATIC
context.note: Maintainers’ catalogue/download interface, observed 28 October 2026. No changing game counts are adopted. https://datomatic.no-intro.org/index.php?page=download

context.title: Jean Louis-Guerin, Interchangeable Preservation Format Documentation
context.note: Version 1.6, April 2018, sections 1.1–1.5: preservation workflow, raw captures, analysed descriptions and IPF. Independent technical investigation, explicitly not an official error-free SPS specification. https://www.kryoflux.com/download/ipf_documentation_v1.6.pdf

context.title: KryoFlux stream protocol documentation
context.note: Jean Louis-Guérin, revision 1.1, 1 December 2013: raw stream records and timing layer, distinct from analysed IPF. https://www.kryoflux.com/download/kryoflux_stream_protocol_rev1.1.pdf

context.title: WinUAE, Basic features
context.note: Consumer project lists IPF among supported floppy formats. https://www.winuae.net/features/
